PullRequest.Title: sessions: add cloud automation cards and run history
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

Wave5, stacked on #340420 (`bevillal/cloud-automations-dialog`). The latest wave4 dialog and central GitHub client implementation remain authoritative.

- Present cloud automation cards with repository metadata, local-time schedules, and an Open on GitHub definition link.
- Render cloud run history with repository/status/relative timestamps; keep native and cloud rows interleaved in run-start order as sessions resolve.
- Move Refresh into the view header. Keep background refresh quiet, preserve cached history on failures, and only claim an empty history once the catalogue is ready.
- Refresh active cloud history every 15 seconds, with bounded discovery after dispatch; do not poll idle definition catalogues.
- Preserve keyboard focus, accessible content, gated visibility, account/client invalidation, and mutation uncertainty.

Native cloud-session resolution, sidebar provenance/filtering, read/unread, archive, follow-up conversations, and agent tools remain outside this wave.

## Validation

Windows, fnm Node 24.18.0:

- `npm run build-fast` — passed (client, built-in extensions and Copilot).
- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed.
- `npm run valid-layers-check` — passed.
- Targeted `npm run eslint -- <changed TypeScript paths>` and `npm run stylelint -- src\vs\sessions\contrib\sessions\browser\media\automationsCards.css` — passed; CSS reports ten pre-existing design-token suggestions.
- Non-action selection below — 152 passing in Electron and 152 passing in Chromium, zero failures:

```powershell
$nonAction = 'refresh|catalogue|catalogues|history|schedule|focus|readiness|account|credential|grant|lifetime|default-off|gates|public|private|discovery|discover|identity|temporary|poll|visibility|incomplete|unavailable|unknown|unsupported state|cloud cards|target|accessible|templates|metadata|date|run status|needs-input'
.\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\sessions\contrib\sessions\test\browser\automationsView.test.ts --run src\vs\sessions\contrib\providers\copilotChatSessions\test\browser\cloudAutomationStore.test.ts --run src\vs\sessions\contrib\providers\copilotChatSessions\test\browser\githubCloudAutomationStore.test.ts --run src\vs\sessions\contrib\automations\test\browser\providerAutomationService.test.ts --grep $nonAction
npm run test-browser-no-install -- --browser chromium --runGlob '**/sessions/contrib/{sessions,providers/copilotChatSessions,automations}/test/browser/{automationsView,cloudAutomationStore,githubCloudAutomationStore,providerAutomationService}.test.js' --grep $nonAction
```

- Twelve non-mutating component-fixture scenarios passed DOM/focus assertions and screenshots: empty, initial loading, unavailable, catalogue error, partial loading/error, dark/light/high-contrast cloud history, narrow background loading, retained history after error, and first-load failure without cached rows. No fixture page errors.
- Live read-only OSS validation: one manual Refresh produced one definition read and one history read, history stayed at the exact same vertical position, and 61 seconds with terminal-only history produced zero idle definition/history requests. Temporary observation hooks were removed.
- `.\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\common\automations\schedule.test.ts` — 14 passing, including timezone/weekday rollover.
- Regression observed before fixing: incomplete catalogues incorrectly showed “No runs yet”; the new test failed before the readiness guard and passes afterward.
- Maintainer verified enable/disable, deletion, and GitHub-side creation followed by Refresh. Actions were not the focus of this validation pass.

## Copilot review

All three wave5 findings were accepted and addressed in `358a1a87351`:

- Accessible “No runs” now requires a ready catalogue/history and existing automations.
- First-load history failure no longer claims cached history exists.
- Architecture documentation keeps the stable bounded-discovery contract; exact cadence/retry counts remain in focused implementation tests.

Both behavior regressions were reproduced with failing tests before the fixes. These are findings from this PR's review, not wave4's review.

## Manual testing

1. Launch the Agents window and enable `chat.automations.enabled` and `chat.automations.cloud.enabled`.
2. Open Automations. Confirm repository metadata and locally converted daily/weekly schedules.
3. Observe an active cloud run and manual Refresh: history stays in place and no loading message pushes rows downward.
4. Inspect empty, failed, and partial catalogue/history fixture states; failures retain cached data and do not masquerade as confirmed empty.
5. Navigate cards and mixed history by keyboard. Resolve a new local session and confirm older cloud rows do not jump above it.
6. Compare dark, light, high-contrast, and narrow layouts.

## Limitations

- Error/account/race scenarios use deterministic tests or fixtures, not destructive changes to a real GitHub account.
- No real screen-reader audio verification.
- This is a stacked draft PR; inherited wave4 onboarding feedback belongs to #340420. No unrelated dependency lockfile drift is included.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The timer trigger, all-entry mapping, concrete REST methods, concurrency limit, catalogue bounds, and shared sequencer are directly traced. Only the prevalence of very large catalogues is uncertain; the regression already scales poorly for realistic catalogues of dozens.
Findings.PerformanceResource: GitHub REST requests and the shared cloud-store operation sequencer
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Each scheduled tick calls refreshHistory(), which issues one listRuns request for every cached definition and then task-detail requests for every active task returned. Cost is O(D + A) per tick for D definitions and A active tasks, every 15 seconds while any one run is active; definition reads allow up to 1,000 definitions per repository and remembered repositories are not capped.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: excessive network traffic and increased latency for run, stop, update, and delete operations queued behind the poll
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this change, the catalogue-wide history fan-out ran only during explicit/initial refresh; one active run did not repeatedly reread every unrelated definition.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The added scheduler repeatedly invokes the existing catalogue-wide history refresh whenever any run is pending/running or discovery attempts remain.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added condition at line 203 schedules another 15-second refresh based on a single active run; the scheduler callback added at lines 44-48 invokes refreshHistoryInBackground(), moving the pre-existing all-definition fan-out onto a recurring path.
Findings.Title: Poll only definitions that can change
Findings.Impact: With dozens of cloud automations and one active run, every tick sends dozens of REST calls at concurrency 4. GitHubCloudAutomationStore serializes refreshHistory and mutations through the same Sequencer, so a long poll also delays user-triggered run/stop/update actions; the new post-dispatch discovery performs the same full fan-out immediately plus four more ticks.
Findings.Evidence: CloudAutomationStore schedules this path whenever runs contains any pending/running item. refreshHistory() in GitHubCloudAutomationStore maps every cachedEntries entry to client.automations.listRuns(...), limits only concurrency to 4, and performs client.tasks.get for active tasks. Both refreshHistory() and mutate() use this.operations.queue(), proving contention with mutations. listDefinitions permits ten pages of 100 definitions per repository, while persisted repositories have no cap.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep the active/discovery set by automation ID and refresh only definitions with active cached runs plus the definition just dispatched/stopped. Remove IDs when their runs become terminal; retain a separately bounded/manual full-catalogue refresh for reconciliation.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The one-tree-per-block behavior and constructor cost are explicit, and tests intentionally cover multiple segmented lists. Exact render time depends on history composition and hardware, so severity is medium rather than high.
Findings.PerformanceResource: WorkbenchObjectTree instances, SessionItemRenderer objects, DOM nodes, event listeners, and synchronous layout work
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For an alternating sequence of cloud and native runs in one date group, the new segmentation creates O(B) SessionsFlatList/WorkbenchObjectTree instances where B can approach the number of native runs; before the PR there was one list instance per date group.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: higher synchronous render/layout latency and retained UI memory when opening or updating mixed run history
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The previous group representation owned one listContainer and lazily created at most one SessionsFlatList for all native session rows in that date group, with temporary rows rendered separately.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: updateGroupRuns now splits native sessions at every external row and calls createSessionList for each contiguous native block.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added block at line 1394 calls createSessionList(entry.runsContainer) inside the per-block traversal; deleted code in createGroup/ensureGroupList maintained a single entry.list for the entire date group.
Findings.Title: Avoid one tree widget per interleaved run block
Findings.Impact: A realistic mixed history with many interleaved local and cloud runs constructs dozens of independent tree controls. Each SessionsFlatList creates a SessionItemRenderer and a WorkbenchObjectTree with service wiring and listeners, so history opening and polling updates become substantially heavier than rendering the same rows in a single control.
Findings.Evidence: The new loop changes listKey after every non-session row and creates a SessionsFlatList whenever that keyed block is absent. SessionsFlatList's constructor synchronously creates SessionItemRenderer, SessionsTreeDelegate, WorkbenchObjectTree, DOM, and multiple listeners. Cloud history can contribute up to 50 rows per definition, making alternating blocks realistic and not a fixed small count.
Findings.Recommendation: Represent the date group with one mixed list/tree (custom elements for external rows and session elements for native rows), or use a lightweight shared session-row renderer so ordering does not require a separate WorkbenchObjectTree for every contiguous native block.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the Automations view or invoke Refresh
Scenarios.CriticalPath: View-entry refresh is fire-and-forget and does not block initial rendering; the manual Refresh command awaits the same operation before completing.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Validate each repository, page user-owned automation summaries, and fetch each definition detail.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Per refresh: one repository query plus up to 10 list pages and one detail request per definition for each deduplicated repository.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The cloud provider performed initial/explicit refreshes, but constructing the view did not itself request another refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the initial view-render critical path; awaited by manual Refresh and precedes history refresh.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: List up to 50 runs for every cached definition and fetch detail for active tasks.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: D listRuns requests plus A task-detail requests, with four definition pipelines active at once.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: History was read during provider initial/explicit refresh, not additionally on view construction.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited by manual Refresh; view-entry invocation is background work.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Deduplicated known/recent repositories R, definitions D across those repositories, and active task rows A returned in the 50-row windows.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Definition catalogue work is sequential by repository, definition details are fetched in groups of 5, history pipelines run at concurrency 4, and duplicate provider refresh/history calls coalesce through refreshPromise/historyRefresh.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The GitHub client and catalogue/history rows are retained, but explicit refresh revalidates repositories and definitions and rereads history. Concurrent refreshes coalesce; failures retain cached history.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the entry call, provider call graph, request loops, and coalescing fields are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Repository and definition counts vary, and in-flight provider initialization can coalesce the added view-entry refresh.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: entry refresh is intentional and off initial rendering; concurrent startup work coalesces. The recurring fan-out is covered by the polling finding.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each poll is background for display updates, but the complete history refresh occupies the same operation sequencer used by mutations.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: List run history for every cached cloud definition and fetch active task details.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: D + A REST calls per completed 15-second cycle; D can reach 1,000 per repository and remembered repositories are uncapped.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Before the PR, one active run did not schedule repeated catalogue-wide history reads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Background for rendering, but blocks run/stop/update/delete queued on the shared Sequencer until the full fan-out completes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: All cached definitions D, not just definitions with active runs, plus active task details A; ticks recur after completion every 15 seconds while any run is active.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: At most one provider history refresh is in flight; each refresh uses four concurrent definition pipelines. Polls do not overlap, but all mutations serialize behind the current refresh.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cached rows avoid an empty UI and survive errors, but do not suppress any listRuns/task-detail request on a successful tick. A failure stops automatic retries until manual refresh.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: timer reachability, all-entry request mapping, limiter, and shared sequencer are directly shown.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical user catalogue size and GitHub round-trip duration are not measured; dozens of definitions are sufficient to produce repeated bursts and sequencer delay.

Scenarios.Scenario: Dispatch or stop a cloud automation and discover the resulting state
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The dispatch/abort request is awaited for acknowledgement. Discovery starts immediately afterward in the background, but can delay subsequent mutations through the shared sequencer.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch an automation or abort a task.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same single dispatch/abort boundary existed before this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: On the user action's acknowledgement path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Perform immediate and four delayed catalogue-wide history refreshes for discovery.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Five rounds of D listRuns plus active-detail requests after each acknowledged or indeterminate action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Dispatch/stop did not trigger bounded automatic history discovery.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the acknowledgement path after dispatch/stop, but contends with following user mutations.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One targeted user action triggers one immediate full-catalogue history read plus four scheduled full-catalogue reads; each read scales with D definitions and A active task details.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Dispatch/abort and history refreshes are globally serialized by the store Sequencer; each history refresh internally runs four definition pipelines.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The discovery counter is bounded and concurrent history requests coalesce, but cached history does not narrow discovery to the affected definition.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: tests assert five history reads and implementation sets four attempts after the immediate refresh.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The affected definition may appear on the first attempt, but the current counter still schedules the remaining attempts while discoveryAttempts is positive.
Scenarios.Verdict: Covered by the catalogue-wide polling fan-out finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render mixed local-session and external cloud run history
Scenarios.CriticalPath: All grouping, widget construction, DOM insertion, tree population, and list layout run synchronously during reactive history rendering.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Visible runs grouped by date and the number B of contiguous native-session blocks created by interleaving external rows; B can approach the number of native runs.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single UI thread; no deferred construction or shared list across blocks.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Groups, temporary rows, and keyed session blocks are retained between updates, but every previously unseen block eagerly constructs a separate list/tree. Poll updates reuse stable blocks when ordering is unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the traversal keying and SessionsFlatList constructor directly prove one WorkbenchObjectTree per native block.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Worst-case alternation depends on users having both local and cloud runs on the same date; the new product explicitly interleaves those sources and cloud reads allow 50 rows per definition.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium-severity rendering and retained-UI regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Update cloud row timestamps/status and use external links/actions
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Status reconciliation synchronously updates row DOM, hovers, toolbar state, and layout; opening GitHub is user initiated and outside render progress.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Hand an external GitHub URL to the opener/browser.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One handoff per explicit user activation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: External cloud definitions/runs had no opener action in this view.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only the explicit open action waits for the handoff; it is not on rendering or polling critical paths.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of visible external rows C; each owns a toolbar and a one-minute timestamp timer.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: UI updates run serially on the main thread; timers fire independently once per minute per external row.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Rows are keyed and retained, while hover registrations are replaced on each row update. No network cache is involved in opener actions.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the per-row work, lower for material user impact at expected row counts.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The cost of per-row timers, toolbar updates, and hover replacement is smaller than the independent tree proliferation and no concrete jank threshold is established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding; the concrete mixed-history cost is captured by the per-block tree finding.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance review over all 15 changed files. Submitted two findings: catalogue-wide REST polling on a shared mutation sequencer, and eager construction of one full session tree per interleaved native block. No qualifying performance-regression fix was identified.
